figures.caption: Three-seed performance of the acquisition-specific configurations. Small circles show the actual outcomes for seeds 0, 1, and 2; larger markers and bars show mean ± sample SD. Each cohort has its own labelled AP axis. Pano includes combined center–shape scoring. No between-model improvement or statistical superiority is inferred from these within-configuration error bars.

Mobile framework-level AP comparison. Labels identify each detector and its AP. Error bars show sample SD only for the three-seed DENT-STRIDE-Mobile, official DEIM-s, and RT-DETRv2-S entries; other methods are single-seed observations. Input resolution, pretraining, and native training/output settings differ across frameworks, as specified in Section 4.6. The plot describes system performance rather than an isolated identity-module effect.

HOOA branch comparison on the same smartphone images. Independently trained seed-0 models retain the same training protocol and differ only in the high-pass and second-order branches. Columns show the original image, ground truth, three branch-removal configurations, and full HOOA; lower rows show identical target enlargements. Teal boxes are ground truth and orange boxes are predictions retained at score ≥0.30. (A) The highlighted reference tooth is FDI 41; No high-pass: FDI 42, 14 correct matches and 7 false positives; No second-order: FDI 42, 14 correct matches and 10 false positives; Neither branch: FDI 42, 10 correct matches and 15 false positives; Full HOOA: FDI 41, 16 correct matches and 7 false positives. (B) The highlighted reference tooth is FDI 81; No high-pass: FDI 41, 10 correct matches and 9 false positives; No second-order: FDI 41, 10 correct matches and 5 false positives; Neither branch: FDI 41, 11 correct matches and 10 false positives; Full HOOA: FDI 81, 13 correct matches and 6 false positives. These selected examples illustrate branch effects; the complete validation ablation determines their aggregate AP differences.

Four-way anatomical scoring at identical Pano weights. (A) AP and (B) AR100. Small circles show the actual outcomes of the three seed-specific checkpoints under no prior, center, shape, and combined scoring. Larger markers and bars show mean ± sample SD. All scores are recomputed before native top-k selection; weights and predicted box coordinates are unchanged.

Same-weight DENTEX anatomical-prior comparison. The same seed-2 checkpoint is evaluated without a prior, with center scoring, with shape scoring, and with both. Scores are recomputed from all ordinary query–class candidates before native top-k selection; box coordinates do not change. Original images and reference annotations are accompanied by identical target enlargements. Teal boxes denote ground truth and orange boxes predictions retained at score ≥0.30. (A) At the same query box, the highest retained label changes from FDI 46 to FDI 45 for reference FDI 45; image-level correct matches change from 19 to 20. (B) At the same query box, the highest retained label changes from FDI 47 to FDI 48 for reference FDI 47; image-level correct matches change from 25 to 24. The favorable and adverse examples illustrate score-ranking effects rather than a change in learned localization.

Retrained HOOA and factor-supervision ablations. Bars report AP differences after each branch or supervision-target removal. HOOA uses the full Mobile seed-0 configuration (54.910 AP); factor supervision uses all three targets with training and inference fusion disabled (55.537 AP). Every tested removal is shown. These single-seed results have no uncertainty bars.

Same-image mobile detector comparison. Columns show the original image, ground truth, official DEIM-s, RT-DETR-L, and DENT-STRIDE; each lower row uses the same target enlargement. Teal boxes denote reference annotations and orange boxes model predictions retained at score ≥0.30. FDI labels identify the highlighted localization match. (A) Reference FDI 32; Official DEIM-s: FDI 72, 8 correct matches and 4 false positives; RT-DETR-L: FDI 72, 7 correct matches and 7 false positives; DENT-STRIDE: FDI 32, 11 correct matches and 0 false positives. Frameworks retain their native training and output-processing settings; this is a system-level comparison, not an isolated module ablation. The selected improvement and adverse examples do not estimate population frequencies.

Actual CMFA/HOOA forward-pass responses for the same Mobile image shown in Fig. 8A. CMFA channel gates gA/gB are arranged as 16 × 16 channel-index grids; Gs is the spatial gate. HOOA panels show local, context, high-pass, second-order, channel/spatial gates, input, and output. Sigmoid gates use their actual [0,1] values. Response RMS maps are divided by their respective 99th percentile and clipped to [0,1]. These are native internal tensors, not Grad-CAM or causal evidence from visualization alone.

Normalized width and height distributions of the 16,234 DENTEX training boxes, grouped by the 32 permanent FDI classes. The distributions describe training geometry; the SpatialShape shape term uses the joint regularized quadratic score of log-width and log-height. No validation boxes are used to fit these templates.

Complete component-sensitivity plots for settings not emphasized in main Fig. 11. All displayed points are seed-0 observations, without uncertainty bars. ΔAP uses the group-specific reference in Table S2 or the factor-fusion-off reference in Table S5. Positive values indicate an alternative that exceeds the reference; they are not gains attributed to the intact module.

Same-checkpoint center, shape, and combined prior effects. Points show the mean paired AP difference versus no prior and bars show exploratory Student-t 95% intervals over the three seeds (df = 2). The zero line denotes no AP change. Intervals are conditional on validation-selected weights and are not patient-sampling or independent-test intervals.

Detection and threshold diagnostics for the final seed-0 configurations. Rows show Pano, Mobile, and DSLR. Columns show category-macro-averaged COCO interpolated precision at IoU 0.50 and maxDets = 100, F1, and raw duplicate-image rate. Unsupported categories are omitted from the precision average. Thresholds range from 0.05 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05; dotted lines indicate 0.30. These are cohort-level detection diagnostics, not clinical charting-error estimates.

Complete Pano FDI outcome matrix and class support for the final seed-0 configuration. Each reference tooth contributes one predicted FDI or a missed outcome; colors show reference-row percentages. The matrix contains 1,861 reference teeth: 1,708 correct identities, 131 wrong-FDI localization matches, and 22 missed teeth. The 164 unmatched predictions are counted separately, not assigned a reference row. Training support totals 16,234 teeth. Gray rows have no validation support and are unavailable, not zero-accuracy classes.

Complete Mobile FDI outcome matrix and class support for the final seed-0 configuration. Each reference tooth contributes one predicted FDI or a missed outcome; colors show reference-row percentages. The matrix contains 2,459 reference teeth: 2,177 correct identities, 166 wrong-FDI localization matches, and 116 missed teeth. The 480 unmatched predictions are counted separately, not assigned a reference row. Training support totals 9,837 teeth. Gray rows have no validation support and are unavailable, not zero-accuracy classes.

Complete DSLR FDI outcome matrix and class support for the final seed-0 configuration. Each reference tooth contributes one predicted FDI or a missed outcome; colors show reference-row percentages. The matrix contains 2,742 reference teeth: 2,599 correct identities, 71 wrong-FDI localization matches, and 72 missed teeth. The 222 unmatched predictions are counted separately, not assigned a reference row. Training support totals 10,760 teeth. Gray rows have no validation support and are unavailable, not zero-accuracy classes.

Validation AP trajectories over the full 160-epoch training budget for the three acquisition-specific configurations. Thin lines show actual seeds 0, 1, and 2; thick lines and bands show their epoch-wise mean ± sample SD. Curves show the recorded trajectory without smoothing or synthetic interpolation, and do not replace selected-checkpoint endpoints.

Prototype representation diagnostics from the final Mobile seed-0 checkpoint. (A) Cosine similarity between normalized class-centroid prototypes ordered by FDI quadrant. (B) Within-class four-prototype cosine cohesion, grouped by quadrant. Gray unsupported slots are unavailable. The prototype bank supplies training supervision only and is distinct from fixed anatomical templates.

Per-class prototype cohesion for permanent and primary FDI slots in the final Mobile seed-0 checkpoint. Cohesion averages the six pairwise cosine similarities among four prototypes. Unsupported classes 18, 28, 38, and 48 are unavailable. No inference prototype score is added to detection logits.

Row-normalized auxiliary quadrant, tooth-position, and dentition confusion matrices for 2,341 localized unique ordinary queries from the final Mobile seed-0 checkpoint. Gray rows have no reference observations. These branches supervise structured identity, not objectness. Their unique-query matching protocol is distinct from post-top-k detector endpoints.
